_comment: Folder B. The house rules, and nothing else. This file declares them; the .rq files under sparql/ implement them. It is deliberately NOT a copy of the suite's registry.json -- folder-a-fleet-project/merge_registry.py joins the two at run time, so the suite's own entries stay whatever the installed suite says they are. See ../README.md.
_owner: Fleet Data Standards group -- raise changes as a PR here, not in a project that consumes it

checks.title: Vehicle asset tag missing or not in the house format
checks.description: Every vehicle on the fleet register must carry an asset tag of the form FLT-NNNNNN. The tag is the key the maintenance system, the finance ledger and the telematics feed all join on, so a vehicle without one in the agreed format cannot be reconciled against any of them. No suite check can know this format: it is a local convention, which is why it lives here.
checks.remediation: Set :assetTag to the tag printed on the vehicle's chassis plate, formatted FLT- followed by six digits. If the vehicle genuinely has no plate yet, it is not yet on the register and should not be in this dataset.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every vehicle carries a well-formed asset tag

checks.title: Retired vehicle still has an open work order
checks.description: A vehicle whose status is Retired has a work order against it that is still Open. One of the two is wrong: either the vehicle was retired with maintenance outstanding, or the work order was never closed when it was. Both cost money -- the first strands a part on order, the second keeps a bay allocated to a vehicle that has left the fleet.
checks.remediation: Close the work order if the work was done or cancelled, or put the vehicle back to InService if it was retired in error. If a retired vehicle really does need work before disposal, model that explicitly rather than leaving an operational work order open.
checks.cucumber_scenario: No retired vehicle has outstanding work

checks.title: Vehicle is not assigned to a depot
checks.description: An in-service vehicle with no :operatesFrom depot appears in no depot's capacity figures and on no depot's rota. Info rather than Warning because the register is the system of record for ownership, not for day-to-day allocation, and a vehicle between depots legitimately has none for a short while.
checks.remediation: Set :operatesFrom to the depot the vehicle is allocated to. If it is genuinely unallocated, that is worth knowing and this finding is the record of it.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every in-service vehicle has a home depot
